description:
FILED s483c (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1620 probe batteries (rows 17/18 of
probes/p1620.pl and row 56 of probes/p1620c.pl).  PRE-EXISTING: byte-identical
on main 6eea8578 and on the s483c tree -- #1620's fix does not touch it (that
one is the ARROW arms; this is the no-arrow subscript arm, whose reading is
right and whose RUNTIME is not).

An element access through a reference that is NOT the right container kind
must be perl's fatal.  Two spellings, two different wrong answers:

    use strict; use warnings;
    my %h = (k => 'v'); my $hr = \%h; my $hrr = \$hr;   # a REF, not a HASH
    my @a = (10, 11);   my $ar = \@a; my $arr = \$ar;   # a REF, not an ARRAY
    print eval { $$hrr{k} } // 'undef', " [$@]\n";
    print eval { $$arr[0] } // 'undef', " [$@]\n";

    perl 5.40.3:  undef [Not a HASH reference at ...]
                  undef [Not an ARRAY reference at ...]
    PCL        :  undef [Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is
                         #S(p-box :...) which is not of type HASH-TABLE]
                  undef []                      <-- no error AT ALL

So the hash half LEAKS A HOST ERROR into user-visible output (an SBCL type
error naming `sb-impl::gethash3` -- the IR-host-leak family, at run time),
and the array half is SILENT: the eval succeeds and the program continues
with undef where perl would have died.  Same family as #1592/#1618 (the
"deref of the wrong kind is perl's fatal" campaign), on the subscript arm.

WHERE: the `a_ref_acc` / `h_ref_acc` runtime path (`p-aref` / `p-gethash`
with a box-valued container argument).  The emission is correct -- the
outermost cast picks the access kind, which is what perl does; it is the
runtime that must raise perl's message when the dereferenced value is not
an ARRAY/HASH.  Note `$$hrr{k}` and `$$arr[0]` reach it through a p-box
holding a REF, so the check is "what does this box HOLD", not "is this a
box".

BAR: the #1592/#1618 recipe -- one runtime arm per container kind with
perl's message, ~10 probe shapes (both wrong-kind directions, a CODE ref,
a GLOB, a plain string = the symbolic-ref path, which must KEEP working),
a guard row beside the #1618 rows in Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t, the full sweep
(a `cl/` change is invisible to corpus-diff) and the op/ companion leg.
SIZE: S-M.

=== DONE (s484a) ===

SHIPPED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13).  ONE predicate was asking the wrong question.

`%p-scalar-referent-p` -- "is this a reference to a plain SCALAR" -- required
the referent scalar to hold a PLAIN value:

    (and (p-box-p r) (not (%p-referent-shaped-p (p-box-value r))))

so a `\$hr` (a scalar HOLDING a hashref) answered NIL and none of the fourteen
container-deref sites that consult it raised the fatal.  perl asks only about
the referent's TYPE -- an SV holding an RV is still an SV -- so the second
conjunct is gone and the predicate is now `(p-box-p (%p-ref-referent val))`.

THE NARROWER QUESTION IS REAL AND HAS EXACTLY ONE ASKER: reftype's SCALAR vs
REF (#1619, fixed in s483b the same day).  It became
`%p-plain-scalar-referent-p`, documented as the broad predicate's strict
subset.  Widening the shared predicate WITHOUT splitting would have re-broken
#1619 within hours -- that is the finding, not the fix.

TWO MORE ARMS in the same family:
  * `%p-designator-hash` / `%p-designator-array` -- the ONE resolver for
    exists/delete -- raise the fatal, so `exists $$hrr{k}` stops answering a
    quiet NO and `delete $$hrr{k}` stops crashing SBCL's GETHASH.  Four
    element primitives, one check; the callers' `%p-wrong-referent-p` sees only
    the unboxed value and cannot diagnose a p-box.
  * `%p-wrong-referent-p` counts a COMPILED REGEXP for every kind: `@$qr` was
    the stringified pattern as a one-element list, `%$qr` zero keys, `$$qr[0]`
    undef, `$$qr{k}` a host error.  perl: `Not a ... reference`, all five.

A TYPEGLOB still does not count, and that is NOT an oversight: a glob VALUE in
container position IS perl's glob slot (`@{*main::gl}` is `@main::gl`), so only
a glob REF is the fatal and telling them apart needs the BOX.  Filed as #1638
with its 17-row probe table.

PROBES, 40 shapes vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s484a/probes/p1628.pl) -- 38
IDENTICAL, the two that differ are #1638's:
  wrong-kind READ both directions (hash-thru-REF/ARRAY/CODE/SCALAR and the
  array twins), the RIGHT kind still working, the WRITE side, exists/delete
  through a wrong-kind ref, whole-aggregate `@$arr`/`%$hrr` (which answered
  `ARRAY(0x1)` and 0), nested `$$$arrr[0]` and `${$$arr}[0]`, the arrow
  `$arr->[0]`, a GLOB ref, a qr//, the SYMBOLIC-ref path (4 rows, must keep
  working), and undef autovivification (4 rows, must NOT die).

COST: arrhash 0.0804 -> 0.0788 s, slices 0.1113 -> 0.1084, arrhash-k 0.0592 ->
0.0599 (tools/bench-exec.pl, best-of-5, quiet box, load < 1) -- nothing outside
noise.  The broad predicate is CHEAPER (one call fewer), and the designators'
new test is one `p-box-p` on a warm path where the value is the hash table.

GUARD `Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t` 39 -> 45.  Rows 40-42 + 44 FAIL on a `2ffefb36`
archive extraction; rows 43 (the symbolic-ref path) and 45 (reftype's SCALAR vs
REF) pass on BOTH trees by design -- that is what a negative row is for.
The fixtures are spelled in TWO statements, never `\(my $hr = \%h)`, because
that shape loses the whole-aggregate fatal on its own (#1639, pre-existing and
measured on both trees); the file says so in a header comment.

BARS: full sweep + the op/ companion leg (a `cl/` change is invisible to
corpus-diff), `tools/ir-host-leak.pl` byte-identical to base, `tools/ir-conform`
clean.  Numbers in DECIDED.md sec s484a and the session log.

ALSO FILED: #1639 (the `\(my $hr = \%h)` declaration shape).
subject: element access through a wrong-kind reference is not perl's fatal: `$$hrr{k}` leaks a raw SBCL gethash3 error, `$$arr[0]` returns undef with NO error
